headline: 5 Ethereum contracts catalogued from official deployments; Arbitrum and Optimism deployments not found.

findings.text: D1: Etherscan search surfaced the Ethereum Entrypoint proxy / Deposit contract; direct searchHandler probes for Etherscan, Arbiscan, and Optimism explorer were blocked by fetch allowlisting.
D2: Official Privacy Pools deployments documentation lists five Ethereum Mainnet contracts: Entrypoint proxy, Entrypoint implementation, PrivacyPool ETH, WithdrawalVerifier, and RagequitVerifier.
D3: No audit links were pinned in the run context; the core GitHub repository exposes an audit folder, but the fetched page did not render auditable file entries.
D4: GitHub source repositories were found, but no content-addressed deployment artifact at a pinned commit SHA was fetched.
D5: The official deployments page only rendered Ethereum Mainnet deployments despite the pinned chain list including Ethereum, Arbitrum, and Optimism.
D6: No factory address was surfaced, so no factory-child enumeration was performed.
D7: All catalogued addresses use the controlled role vocabulary with actor_class set to unknown because Safe/EOA/bytecode classification was not read.
D8: Every address included in protocol_metadata.admin_addresses is backed by the official deployments page.

rationale.verdict: Discovery catalogued five Ethereum contracts from official docs and one corroborating Etherscan page; Arbitrum, Optimism, audit-era, factory-child, and pinned-commit deployment artifacts remain unresolved.

evidence.shows: Official deployments page states it contains deployed Privacy Pools contract addresses and lists Ethereum Mainnet Entrypoint Proxy 0x6818809eefce719e480a7526d76bd3e561526b46, Entrypoint Implementation 0xdd8aa0560a08e39c0b3a84bba356bc025afbd4c1, PrivacyPool ETH 0xf241d57c6debae225c0f2e6ea1529373c9a9c9fb, WithdrawalVerifier 0x022891f938ae7fdc8ab9ead0fbf50aba8c897d6d, and RagequitVerifier 0xa45aca8604a73d80c551faad6355a5c3a5565ec6.
Etherscan address page labels 0x6818809eefce719e480a7526d76bd3e561526b46 as Privacy Pools: Deposit, shows it is a verified ERC1967Proxy contract, and shows a proxy constructor implementation field.

Canonical core repository for Privacy Pools; README describes a protocol for private asset transfers where users deposit funds publicly and partially withdraw privately while proving membership in approved address sets.

Canonical website repository; README links to privacypools.com and docs.privacypools.com and describes the UI as enabling deposits and later partial or full withdrawals without an on-chain link between deposit and withdrawal addresses, with ASP validation.

Protocol docs describe PrivacyPool contracts as managing commitments and nullifiers, processing deposits and withdrawals, handling Merkle tree state, validating zero-knowledge proofs, and supporting wind down through the Entrypoint.
Security policy instructs vulnerability reporters to email security@0xbow.io and says a bounty may be offered where applicable.

unknowns: D1: Direct explorer searchHandler fetches for Ethereum, Arbitrum, and Optimism were rejected by the fetch tool allowlist; search grounding found an Ethereum Etherscan page but no Arbitrum or Optimism Privacy Pools address pages.
D2: Official deployments documentation fetched in this run only rendered Ethereum Mainnet addresses; no Arbitrum or Optimism deployments page section was found.
D3: No audit_links were pinned; GitHub audit folder fetch did not render a usable list of audit PDFs or scoped addresses.
D4: No Foundry broadcast, hardhat-deploy, deployments.json, addresses.json, contracts.json, networks.json, or commit-pinned deployments markdown file was fetched at a specific commit SHA.
D5: chain Arbitrum: zero addresses surfaced from official deployments docs, explorer search grounding, and broad web search.
D5: chain Optimism: zero addresses surfaced from official deployments docs, explorer search grounding, and broad web search.
D6: No factory contract was surfaced from D1-D4, so no allPools/getPool/getMarket/getVault read was attempted.
D8: DefiPunkd API surfacer calls for the discovered Entrypoint proxy were rejected by fetch allowlisting, so live owner/admin/implementation reads were not performed.

protocol_metadata.about: Privacy Pools lets users deposit assets publicly and later withdraw partially or fully without creating an on-chain link between the deposit and withdrawal addresses. The protocol uses zero-knowledge proofs, commitments, nullifiers, Merkle tree state, and an Association Set Provider layer to validate eligible deposits. The deployed Ethereum surface found in this run consists of an Entrypoint proxy, an ETH privacy pool, and withdrawal/ragequit verifier contracts.
